title: Fonctions L / Équation fonctionnelle des fonctions L (cas géométrique) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Physically, this sheet is the blank back of a Bourbaki typescript (n° 392: Algèbre commutative, ch. VII, exercises on reflexive lattices and pseudo-null modules). The faint typed text showing through is the exercise transcribed as the 'next page'. The previous and next 'pages' are therefore Bourbaki material and not Grothendieck's own notes. The only Grothendieck content is a short scratch computation in the L-function file (cote 60).

What the computation appears to do. It writes the ratio of the two sides of a functional equation, L(1/(qt))/L(t), as
- a constant δ (an epsilon-type factor), times
- t^χ (χ an Euler characteristic), times
- two telescoping families of factors.

The auxiliary L-functions L_i and L'_i are indexed by a running integer i, from ρ to ρ+n−1. The two families of factors are:
- L'_i(t)/L'_i(p^{(n−i)}t);
- L_i(p^{(n−i)}t)/L_i(t).

The argument shifts by powers of p (the characteristic, presumably with q a power of p, or q = p in this scratch). The second line restates this compactly:
A(t) = δ t^χ ∏_i L'_i(t)/L'_i(p^{n−i}t) · ∏_i L_i(p^{n−i}t)/L_i(t).

Grothendieck then tests the case n = 1. He writes the string L_ρ(t) L_{ρ+1}(t) L'_ρ(pt), brackets two of its terms, and keeps L_ρ(t) L'_ρ(pt). This suggests he is checking which factors cancel or pair up in the smallest case.

Possible interpretations (uncertain):
- L_i and L'_i are L-functions attached to graded pieces (by cohomological degree, or by a filtration or slope-type decomposition) of a cohomology and of its dual.
- The p-power twists are Tate twists, so that the functional equation of the total L-function, L(1/qt) = δ t^χ L(t) up to duality, follows from, or is reformulated as, relations between the pieces.

This is in the spirit of the p-adic picture in which a zeta function factors as a product of unit-root-type L-functions with arguments twisted by p^i (Dwork, Katz). It may equally be a purely ℓ-adic bookkeeping of Tate twists. The page is too fragmentary to decide.

Problem served: understanding or reorganizing the functional equation of L-functions in the geometric case (cote 60). Grothendieck proved this via the ℓ-adic Lefschetz trace formula and Poincaré duality (SGA 5; Bourbaki seminar 279, 1964).
errors: The formula has the same L on both sides of L(1/qt)/L(t). In general the functional equation relates the L-function of a sheaf to that of its dual (twisted), so the relation as written presupposes self-duality, or an implicit convention.

The index and exponent conventions are inconsistent between line 1 and line 2. In line 1 the first factor has p^n t and the last has pt. In line 2 the exponent is written p^{n−i}, which only matches if i is shifted relative to ρ. This is scratch work, not a checked identity.
The substitution t ↦ 1/(qt) is used with twists by p, not q. This is consistent only if q = p or the notation is loose.

ideas.what: Expressing the functional-equation ratio L(1/qt)/L(t) as δ t^χ times telescoping products of auxiliary L-functions with p-power-twisted arguments
ideas.modern_name: Functional equation of ℓ-adic L-functions (epsilon factor, Euler characteristic exponent) / decomposition of zeta into twisted partial L-functions
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (ℓ-adic functional equation, 1964–65); p-adic unit-root decompositions: Dwork, Katz
ideas.where_published: Bourbaki seminar exp. 279 (1964), SGA 5 (functional equation via Poincaré duality); the specific telescoping manipulation: unsure

ideas.what: Test of the identity in the case n=1

deep.surprise_reason: This is a fragmentary scratch computation of factors in the functional equation of geometric L-functions, written on the back of a Bourbaki typescript. Its context and notation are too incomplete to extract any result beyond the well-known functional equation. Nothing indicates a new or uncredited idea.
transcription_corrections: The neighbouring 'pages' (n° 392, exercises on reflexive lattices and on factorial rings) are the typed Bourbaki text on the other side of, or showing through, these reused sheets. They are not Grothendieck's L-function notes. The faint typed text visible through this page is exercise 26 (the 'next page').
The heading is a crossed-out fragment, roughly 'A … p…'.

In line 1 the subscripts should be read ρ, …, ρ+n−1 (written 'ρ+n…'), not 'ρ_{n…}': first bracket L'_ρ(t)/L'_ρ(p^n t) … L'_{ρ+n−1}(t)/L'_{ρ+n−1}(pt); second bracket L_{ρ+n−1}(pt)/L_{ρ+n−1}(t) … L_ρ(p^n t)/L_ρ(t). A small crossed-out 'L_ρ' sits between the factors.
In line 2 the numerator argument is written with overwriting, approximately L_i(p^{ρ+n−i} t) (the exponent was corrected); the denominators are L'_i(p^{ρ+n−i} t) and L_i(t).
In the n=1 line, the underbraces group L_ρ(t) and L'_ρ(pt), with L_{ρ+1}(t) in between.
